stayOverview: Start with City centre for the easiest first Austin stay, then compare Old Town and Waterfront when price, nightlife, quieter evenings or transfer timing matter more than being beside every major sight.
hotelIntro: Austin hotel choice is mostly about repeat journeys: use City centre for sightseeing, Old Town for a different local base, and Waterfront or Airport area when views, parking, airport timing or longer stays matter.
rentalCars: Do not rent a car for central Austin unless parking and traffic are part of the plan; use one mainly for regional day trips.

history.text: In 1730, three Catholic missions from East Texas were combined and reestablished as one mission on the south side of the Colorado River, in what is now Zilker Park, in Austin.

history.label: 19th century
history.text: The city grew throughout the 19th century and became a center for government and education with the construction of the Texas State Capitol and the University of Texas at Austin.
In 1839, the Texas Congress formed a commission to seek a site for the new capital of the Republic of Texas to replace Houston.

history.label: 1870s
history.text: However, as other new railroads were built through the region in the 1870s, Austin began to lose its primacy in trade to the surrounding communities.
The opening of the Houston and Texas Central Railway (H&TC) in 1871 turned Austin into the major trading center for the region, with the ability to transport both cotton and cattle.

history.label: 20th century
history.text: Following the mid-20th century, Austin became established as one of Texas' major metropolitan centers.
In 1940, the destroyed granite dam on the Colorado River was finally replaced by a hollow concrete dam that formed Lake McDonald (now called Lake Austin) and which has withstood all floods since.

history.label: Civic role
history.text: Spanish colonists traveled through the area, though few permanent settlements were created for some time.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: Spanish forts were established in what are now Bastrop and San Marcos.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: Following Mexico's independence, new settlements were established in Central Texas.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: Black communities such as Wheatville, Pleasant Hill, and Clarksville were established, with Clarksville being the oldest surviving freedomtown ‒ the original post-Civil War settlements founded by former African-American slaves ‒ west of the Mississippi.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: The same year, Tillotson Collegiate and Normal Institute (now part of Huston–Tillotson University) opened its doors.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: In addition, the state legislature established the Lower Colorado River Authority (LCRA) that, along with the city of Austin, created the system of dams along the Colorado River to form the Highland Lakes.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: In addition, the much larger Mansfield Dam was built by the LCRA upstream of Austin to form Lake Travis, a flood-control reservoir.
